title: Hosted API accelerator backlog mitigation and admission-control playbook
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Consolidate incident follow-ups from the hosted API accelerator exhaustion event into an actionable playbook. Scope includes immediate throttling adjustments, admission-control redesign, pre-warm/autoscale policy changes, and observability additions to prevent queue head build-up and unfair scheduling across customers.
root_cause_summary: A combination of a sudden multi-tenant traffic spike and a conservative admission-control threshold caused long-lived queues to accumulate on a subset of accelerator nodes. Kernel selection fallbacks and quantized model variants did not trigger fast enough due to circuit-breaker hysteresis; autoscaler lag allowed saturation to persist. Notably, heavy single-tenant bursts amplified head-of-line blocking for other customers.
action_items: Tune admission control: lower queue depth trigger from 300 to 150 tokens and add per-route request caps
Implement fairness-aware dequeue: ensure per-customer token ceilings to prevent head-of-line blocking
Short-circuit fallback: reduce kernel-selection hysteresis so quantized/cheaper variants are eligible after 2s rather than 8s
Autoscaler improvements: add aggressive pre-warm path for bursty slots and reduce scale-up cool-down from 120s to 45s
Runtime metric surface: emit queue_depth_histogram, head_of_line_customer_id (hash), and admission_reject_rate to Grafana
Runbook updates: document step-by-step mitigation playbook and add explicit escalation to SRE on token-rate > 10k/min
Rate-limiting controls: add soft token-rate throttles per API key with configurable grace periods
Chaos test: add synthetic multi-tenant burst scenario to stage tests to validate fallbacks and autoscaler behavior
Customer communications: draft post-incident email for affected customers and create FAQ for sudden throttling behaviors
updates: 2026-02-19: Triage complete; identified admission-control thresholds and autoscaler cool-down as primary risk vectors.

2026-02-26: Observability schema proposal merged to metrics catalog; dashboards for queue depth and per-route rejection rates created (Grafana panel IDs provided in links).
2026-03-02: Autoscaler tuning patch deployed to staging; pre-warm path validated against synthetic bursts. Will schedule prod rollout behind feature flag.
2026-03-06: Decided to reduce kernel-selection hysteresis to 2s after perf trade-off review; implementation in progress (PR 4368).
2026-03-10: Created runbook draft and started on customer communication template; assigned comms to Solutions.
2026-03-10: Flagged remaining tasks: production rollout gating, SRE alert tuning, and post-release validation window (72h).
decision_log: Adopt fairness-aware dequeue vs. strict per-tenant isolation: chose fairness algorithm because strict isolation increases idle capacity; fairness reduces tail without large capacity overhead.
Quantized fallback hysteresis reduced to 2s after cost/latency simulation showed acceptable degradation for heavily quantized paths while preventing prolonged saturation.
Autoscaler cool-down reduced to 45s with constrained pre-warm budgets to avoid oscillation; will monitor for noise and have rollback flag ready.
Soft per-key rate throttles preferred over hard global throttles to allow graceful degradation for high-value customers with an option for early manual override.
